h1: The 8 Best Bagless Self-Emptying Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Bagless Self-Empty Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 bagless self-emptying robot vacuums from Shark, roborock, uninell and Tikom, scored on bin size, mapping and cost.
summary: The Shark AV2501S AI Ultra is the bagless dock to buy for most homes: a HEPA base rated for 30 days, Matrix Clean mapping and a pet hair focus. The roborock Q7 M5+ stretches that to a listed 7 to 9 weeks between empties, which suits low-maintenance households. The uninell is the pick if you want LiDAR on a mid budget. The Shark Navigator pair covers vacuum-only buyers who want no mop to maintain.
intro: A self-emptying robot that still needs bags just moves the chore. You stop emptying the robot and start buying and swapping dock bags, and the cost never ends. Bagless docks solve that by using a reusable bin, but they have a different weakness: the bin must be emptied by hand, and the filter must be cleaned.

We reviewed eight bagless models by what the listing says about bin capacity, filtration, navigation and mopping. The ones with a mop add a cleaning step, and the vacuum-only models skip it. Rankings are drawn from spec sheets and owner reports, with bin interval and filtration weighed ahead of raw suction.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra Robot Vacuum with Matrix Clean, Bagless Self-Empty Base
products.verdict: A 30 day HEPA bagless base, Matrix Clean mapping and a pet hair focus.
products.description:
The AV2501S pairs a 30 day bagless HEPA self-empty base with home mapping through Matrix Clean and a design aimed at pet hair. It is controlled by an app over Wi-Fi.

It takes first place because the HEPA seal keeps dust in, which matters when a bagless bin is emptied by hand. The roborock Q7 M5+ lists a longer interval but not the filtration detail.

Best for homes with pets that want mapping and a clean emptying process. Caveat: 30 days is the shortest window among the better models.
products.idealFor: Pet homes that want clean, bagless emptying.
products.skipIf: You want mopping in the same machine.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, Up to 7-9 Weeks Self-Empty, 10000Pa
products.verdict: Up to 7 to 9 weeks between empties, 10,000Pa and a mop.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ is a vacuum and mop combo with 10,000Pa suction and a reusable bagless bin the listing rates at 7 to 9 weeks per empty. That is the longest stretch here.

It ranks second because the Shark offers better filtration detail and mapping. It beats the Q10 S5+ below on the dock's listed interval.

Best for a household that wants the longest gap between chores. Caveat: the interval depends on pet hair and dust.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: 10,000Pa, mopping and a bagless dock for under $300.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ pairs 10,000Pa suction with mopping and a bagless self-empty dock that uses a reusable bin. The ongoing cost stays low because there are no bags.

It ranks third because the Q7 M5+ lists a longer interval for a similar price. It outranks the vacuum-only Navigators if you want mopping.

Best for carpet and hard floor homes. Caveat: no interval is listed.
products.idealFor: Mixed floors on a mid budget.
products.skipIf: You want the longest empty window.

products.name: uninell Robot Vacuum and Mop, 7000Pa, LiDAR Self-Empty Station
products.verdict: LiDAR navigation, 7000Pa and a bagless station on a mid budget.
products.description:
The uninell uses LiDAR navigation with 7000Pa suction and a bagless self-empty station, plus mopping. LiDAR maps with a laser, which usually gives more consistent coverage than camera or gyroscope mapping.

It ranks fourth because the brand is far less known than Shark or roborock, which makes parts and support a question mark. It is the cheapest way to get LiDAR with a bagless dock.

Best for a mid budget buyer who values mapping. Caveat: lesser known brand.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base, Grey, RV2120AE
products.verdict: A vacuum-only Shark with a bagless base and no mop to maintain.
products.description:
The RV2120AE skips the mop and pairs plain vacuuming with a reusable-bin dock. With no mop tank, there are fewer parts to keep clean.

It ranks fifth because the AV2501S adds mapping and HEPA, and the Q7 M5+ adds a mop. It is the simple pick.

Best for a vacuum-only buyer who wants a known brand. Caveat: listing details are brief.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base, White, AV2110S
products.verdict: The same Navigator platform in white, usually a little cheaper.
products.description:
The AV2110S is a vacuum-only Shark Navigator with a bagless self-empty base in a white finish. It sits on the same platform as the grey RV2120AE.

It ranks sixth only by a hair: it is a sibling of the model above at a slightly lower price. Check both and buy whichever is cheaper.

Best for a vacuum-only buyer who likes the white finish. Caveat: there is no mop.
products.skipIf: You want a different feature set.

products.name: Airzeen Bagless Robot Vacuum and Mop Self-Emptying for Pet Hair, Carpet
products.verdict: Marketed at pet hair and carpet, with a bagless dock and a mop.
products.description:
The Airzeen is a vacuum and mop combo with a bagless self-emptying base, marketed for pet hair and carpet. Pet hair is where bagless docks clog first, so the claim is worth checking.

It ranks seventh because the brand is new and the listing gives few specifics. The Shark and roborock models have a proven record behind them.

Best for a pet and carpet home on a mid budget. Caveat: read owner comments on hair clogs.
products.idealFor: Pet and carpet homes on a mid budget.

products.name: Tikom Robot Vacuum and Mop, Robotic Vacuum Cleaner with Self-Emptying Base
products.verdict: The lowest price here, with a bagless base and a mop.
products.description:
For the least money here, the Tikom bundles a mop with a reusable-bin dock.

It ranks last because the listing gives no suction number, interval or mapping detail. The brand is also less established than Shark or roborock.

Best for a first robot on a tight budget. Caveat: expect fewer details and a lighter feature set.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers on a tight budget.

whatMatters.factor: How a bagless bin is emptied
whatMatters.detail: A bagless dock stores dust in a reusable bin that you tip into the trash. That costs nothing in bags but can release dust. Look for HEPA or sealed in the listing, and plan to do it outdoors or near a bin.

whatMatters.factor: Interval claims depend on your home
whatMatters.detail: A listing that says 7 to 9 weeks assumes light debris. Pet hair fills a bin far faster. Treat the figure as a ceiling, and halve it for a house with pets.
Bagless docks use washable filters that clog over time. Check that the filter is easy to reach and that replacements are sold. Plan to rinse it monthly.
A combo adds a water tank and pad, which means more cleaning. If you already have a mop you like, a vacuum-only robot has fewer parts to maintain.
LiDAR or camera mapping plans straight rows and remembers rooms. Basic robots bounce randomly and cover less. Look for mapping if your home has several rooms.

faq.q: What is a bagless self-emptying robot vacuum?
faq.a: A robot whose dock sucks debris into a reusable bin, not a paper bag. You empty the bin by hand every few weeks.

faq.q: Are bagless docks cheaper to run?
faq.a: Yes, because there are no bags to buy. You do need to wash the filter occasionally.

faq.q: Is the Shark AV2501S worth more than the Navigator?
faq.a: For pets and larger homes, yes: it adds mapping and HEPA. For a single room the Navigator is enough.
Listings range from 30 days on the Shark AV2501S to 7 to 9 weeks on the roborock Q7 M5+. Pets shorten it.
They can when you empty the bin. A HEPA sealed design reduces it, and emptying near a trash can helps.

faq.q: Is the white Navigator different from the grey one?
faq.a: They share the same platform, so the choice is finish and price.

finalTake: For most households, the Shark AV2501S is the bagless self-emptying robot to buy, thanks to HEPA sealing, mapping and a pet hair focus. The roborock Q7 M5+ wins if you want the longest gap between empties, and the uninell is the LiDAR value pick. If you only vacuum, the Shark Navigator pair keeps things simple, and the Tikom is the cheapest way in.
